photos.file: Bromus tectorum (cheatgrass) and Camelina microcarpa (littlepod false flax) - Flickr - Matt Lavin.jpg
photos.desc: The predilection of these two introduced plant species to disturbed dry sites is illustrated by them dominating the soil still attached to an uprooted ponderosa pine tree.
A distinctive annual mustard but occurring roadside and rarely in adjacent sagebrush steppe.
The hairs are branched and sometimes stellate.
The growth form includes erect single stems to bunched ascending stems but always from disturbed ecological settings (e.g., small mammal mounds, road sides, etc.).
